title: The Lord of the Rings Franchise Overview
body:
The Lord of the Rings is a high-fantasy work by J. R. R. Tolkien, published in three volumes in 1954 and 1955, preceded by The Hobbit in 1937 and followed by posthumous volumes edited from his papers. Its film adaptations of the 2000s and 2010s are likewise matters of public release record.

This public edition records only verifiable facts — titles, authors, publication and release years and formats — in original wording, with no copied passages from Tolkien's text.

The companion Signature edition is separate, labeled unofficial fiction with original characters and lands, and it claims no affiliation with the Tolkien estate or other rights holders.

How to use this record: start with the overview, then read the work-by-work records in publication order. Every date and credit below is a public fact; no copyrighted text is reproduced anywhere in this database.

title: The Lord of the Rings Reading and Viewing Order Guide
body:
Recommended public order for the works in this database is publication and release order, beginning with The Hobbit (1937) and ending with The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power (2022). That order follows how the franchise actually reached the public, and it avoids assuming any later reordering.

The full order is: The Hobbit (1937); The Fellowship of the Ring (1954); The Two Towers (1954); The Return of the King (1955); The Silmarillion (1977); The Fellowship of the Ring (film) (2001); The Two Towers (film) (2002); The Return of the King (film) (2003); The Hobbit: An Unexpected Journey (2012); The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power (2022). Each title in that list has its own record in this database with its credited creators and format.

This guide contains facts only. It does not reproduce story text, and it does not claim that any Signature continuation belongs in the official order.
